answer: Catch clones by the mistakes they share. Each epoch the network slips a few hard questions with known answers into every agent's work, the kind most models get wrong in idiosyncratic ways. Independent agents err differently, like boats scattering around a reef. Copies of one model with one prompt make the same wrong turn on the same item, and a spiral of matching errors across many identities is a strong fingerprint. Identities whose error patterns overlap far above chance share one reward, and an operator would have to diversify models and prompts to escape the inlet.
